transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sara Kim (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood Eng), Mark Liu (Beacon ML Eng), Tessa Moreno (Beacon Data Platform), Ravi Patel (Beacon CTO), Jenna (Beacon PM)

Summary: quick perf review, FP8 exploratory notes, INT8 stability check, next steps on quality eval and scripts.

[00:00] Sara: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, can you hear me okay?
[00:05] Mark: yeah loud and clear, thanks sara. we got a handful of folks from our infra side today too.
[00:12] Daniel: hi all, daniel here, i'll run through the perf numbers and then we can go into the sample outputs where we saw diffs.
[00:20] Tessa: quick note we deployed the test AMI in us-east-1 like you asked, so the runs were on A100s and one trial on T4 for latency baseline.
[00:30] Sara: perfect, let's start with the headline numbers. daniel?
[00:33] Daniel: sure, so on the baseline fp16 model on A100 80GB we see median p95 latency per request at 230ms with batching 8 and avg tokens 120. switching to INT8 quant on the same rig reduced p95 to ~160ms and throughput improved about 1.6x.
[00:52] Mark: that matches our rough numbers earlier but good to see the p95 shift. what about T4?
[00:56] Daniel: on the T4 the baseline fp16 p95 was 480ms, INT8 brought it to ~320ms, so similar relative improvement though absolute latency still higher.
[01:07] Sara: nice. and the FP8 runs?
[01:09] Daniel: fp8 is a little more experimental — on the A100 we saw p95 at 150ms in best-case but it's variable, sometimes similar to INT8. FP8 gave slightly higher throughput gains in some sequences, but there were stability issues on certain long-form prompts; the logits sometimes diverged after 600 tokens.
[01:27] Jenna: can you say more about divergence? overall quality drop?
[01:32] Daniel: yeah so for most prompts quality is comparable to fp16, but we found a subset — mainly instruction-following multi-step prompts — where the model on fp8 produced repeated tokens or short-circuited the generation, appears to be numerical underflow/overaccumulation in some layers.
[01:49] Ravi: is that reproducible across seeds?
[01:52] Daniel: mostly, yes. we've reproduced across runs. the pattern suggests certain attention kernels need a higher-precision accumulator.
[02:00] Priya: that's where mixed precision per-layer fallback helps; you keep critical layers in fp16 and quantize others. we tested a per-layer fallback config and it fixed most of the divergence but reduced the throughput gain from fp8.
[02:14] Sara: sounds like a tradeoff — fp8 max perf but more tuning, int8 more stable.
[02:19] Mark: what about quality scores? do we have Rouge/BLEU or human evals?
[02:23] Daniel: we ran automated metrics on a 500-sample bench: INT8 avg semantic-similarity dropped 0.8% relative to fp16 (small), FP8 dropped around 1.6% but variance higher. human spot-checks flagged a few hallucinations in fp8 runs.
[02:40] Tessa: for our production bar, even 1% drop is concerning if it hits critical flows. we need the 2k eval to be confident.
[02:48] Sara: agreed, hence the action for Beacon to run the 2k sample quality eval.
[02:52] Daniel: also worth noting cost deltas: raw token compute cost for INT8 was ~35% lower versus fp16 on A100 when normalized per request; FP8 was ~42% lower in the best-case but with tuning overhead.
[03:05] Mark: those are compelling savings. can you break down where that comes from? is it kernel-level speed, memory bandwidth?
[03:11] Daniel: both — lower memory bandwidth for activations and faster int8 kernels. also we saw reduced kv-cache footprint which helps batching and concurrency.
[03:19] Ravi: any known interruptions with our stack — we're on k8s with upstream Triton for internal tests — will that map?
[03:26] Daniel: triton integrates but some custom kernel selection in our runtime gives a bit more lift; still, you can see meaningful gains on Triton too but probably less out-of-the-box than Redwood runtime. small word: some ops need custom kernels for fp8 to be stable.
[03:41] Jenna: from planning perspective, if we wanted to push INT8 to prod behind Redwood Dedicated, what would be the recommended guardrails?
[03:48] Priya: I'd recommend start with INT8 across non-critical models, enable per-layer monitoring, have automatic fallback for any request that shows entropy drop, and keep fp16 as the canary. we can also run A/B traffic routing via Redwood Console so you can route say 10% of traffic to INT8 and roll up.
[04:05] Mark: do we have an example of the fallback policy?
[04:09] Daniel: yeah I'll share a sample policy — it checks for repeated tokens and token probability drops, if the metric crosses threshold it retries on fp16 or routes to higher-capacity node.
[04:20] Sara: ok daniel to share that. (note: action item)
[04:24] Mark: one operational q: if we use Private deployment, will KMS drives or HSM affect tokenization or quant?
[04:30] Daniel: KMS/HSM only affects key storage/encryption for customer data, no effect on quant. the only infra constraint is if your boxes are older GPUs, some fp8 kernels may not be available.
[04:41] Tessa: got it. we'll check our private racks.
[04:44] Ravi: how about quantization tooling — do we need to re-export models? can we convert on-the-fly?
[04:50] Priya: generally you produce a quantized artifact. for INT8 we have a conversion path that inserts quantizers with calibration; FP8 currently requires a recompile step in our pipeline. daniel will share scripts.
[05:02] Daniel: i'll drop the fp8 conversion repo and a short runbook, it's not fully automated but straightforward.
[05:07] Mark: perfect. on the 2k eval, should we include our critical templates — user prompt templates — to stress test?
[05:12] Sara: yes include those, and any long-context sequences you care about. jenkins note: include a subset of the fine-tuned instr prompts.
[05:20] Jenna: quick question: were there any differences in logits distribution we should be aware of for downstream safety filters?
[05:26] Daniel: good question — we saw a small shift in logit magnitudes on FP8 which slightly changed thresholding for one of your safety heuristics. we'll share the distribution plots; might need to tweak thresholds or run normalization post-logit.
[05:41] Tessa: that'll be important. can you share what changed numerically?
[05:45] Daniel: sure — i'll include histograms and a suggested normalization factor in the artifact pack.
[05:52] Mark: from your internal POV, what's the recommended path for Beacon — INT8 first or FP8 experiment?
[05:58] Sara: pragmatic path is INT8 first (better stability, immediate wins), run FP8 as an optimization track if you need more savings and have engineering bandwidth for tuning.
[06:08] Ravi: ok we prefer that order.
[06:10] Jenna: timeline wise, we want to decide on Dedicated vs Hosted by end of month; how do these perf numbers affect pricing?
[06:17] Sara: we'll update the pricing spreadsheet with token-level cost deltas; INT8 typically shows ~30-40% compute reduction for pricing purposes which can push you toward Dedicated if your committed usage meets thresholds. i'll model both.
[06:30] Mark: any blockers we should call out?
[06:33] Daniel: operationally the main blockers are the fp8 kernel availability on older GPUs and needing to adjust safety thresholds. otherwise it's more tuning and eval.
[06:42] Tessa: we'll check GPU fleet and share region constraints.
[06:45] Sara: great. let's go through a couple sample outputs where you saw issues. daniel, can you share your screen?
[06:50] Daniel: (screen shares) okay here's the 3 examples — prompt A, B, C. prompt A was a multi-step planning prompt where fp8 truncated the plan after a few steps. prompt B had repetition.
[07:04] Mark: yeah I can see the repetition — seems like a loop. any quick fixes?
[07:08] Priya: we tried per-layer fp16 for the attention and it broke the loop.
[07:13] Mark: does that mean we lose most of fp8 perf?
[07:15] Daniel: some, but still better than fp16 in many cases because other layers remain quantized. overall throughput was +1.25x over fp16 with that mixed config on A100.
[07:27] Jenna: can you include config diff when you send scripts?
[07:30] Daniel: yes will include.
[07:32] Sara: ok quick recap before we wrap — action items and owners, daniel you'll share fp8 repo, conversion script, per-layer fallback example, and policy for automated retry. sara will update pricing and send perf spreadsheet. mark/tessa will run 2k eval and check GPU fleet constraints. becca? (no answer)
[07:52] Mark: one last q — how stable is INT8 across model versions? when we roll new weights does quant require re-calibration?
[07:59] Daniel: ideally you recalibrate after a weight update. for small deltas you might be okay but best practice is to run a quick calibration pass; the toolchain supports fast calibration on sample data.
[08:12] Ravi: good to know. ok thanks everyone.
[08:15] Sara: thanks all, we'll send the artifacts and follow up items. next sync same time next week?
[08:21] Mark: same time works.
[08:23] Sara: great, end call.

Notes on transcript quality: automated ASR had a few mis-labels (e.g., 'fp eight' transcribed as 'f p aight' in raw) and some speaker tags were generic in the raw export. We normalized names where possible.
